sentences.text:
Mr.Vipul Lamba, A  respondents No.2   respondent in per  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGESH KHANNA  ORDER % 20.01.2023 1.

Petitioners file these petitions for quashing of the FIR No.373/2017 under Section 287/304A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Hari Nagar, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.

2. The aforesaid FIR was got registered on an information by one Sunil Kumar regarding an incident dated 03.09.2017 of electrocution and death of one Arun @ Ashok, aged about 19 years; son of respondent No.2 and brother of respondents No.3 & 4.

The learned counsel for petitioners submits the matter has since been settled with the legal heirs of deceased viz respondents No.2 to 4 as mentioned in the memo of parties and there is no other legal heir of deceased.
3. The deceased Arun @ Ashok was working in the banquet hall belonging to the petitioners herein as also by one Naresh Bansal.
The co- accused Naresh Bansal has since settled the matter with the legal heirs of deceased in a plea bargaining proceeding per copy of orders dated 02.11.2019 passed by the learned Trial Court.

Accused Naresh Bansal has paid compensation of Rs.4.00 Lacs to the legal heirs of deceased and has pleaded guilty upon which a lenient view was taken against him and Manish Bansal; Vijender Kumar Gupta ...

he was released on probation for a period of two years.

It is stated Naresh Bansal was looking after the entire affairs of the banquet hall and petitioners herein were never involved in the functioning of the banquet hall and both were merely lessee along with Naresh Bansal of such hall.
4. Admittedly, the informant on whose statement the FIR was registered has not been impleaded in these petitions.
5. Pursuant to settlement dated 21.10.2019, petitioner(s) agreed to pay Rs.4.00 lacs to respondents No.2 to 4.

Out of said sum, the petitioner - Vijender Kumar has already paid Rs.2.00 Lacs to respondents No.2 to 4 and for the balance amount, the petitioners has handed over two drafts No.216089 dated 19.01.2023 drawn on Federal Bank; No523418 dated 03.11.2022 drawn on ICICI Bank both for Rs.1.00 Lacs each in favour of respondent No.2, which have been accepted by her on behalf of all respondents No.2 to 4.
6.
In all, the respondents No.2 to 4 have received total compensation of Rs.8.00 Lacs from petitioners and accused Naresh Bansal.

7. The respondents No.2 to 4 have been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and they have no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

8. Reference is made to WP(Crl) 550/2020 Taranjeet Singh V. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi)
delivered on 13.03.2020 passed by this Court:
6. .....In Kamal Kishore vs. The State (NCT of Delhi) and Ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
the following was held:
"9.

It is a well settled law that where the High Court is convinced that the offences are entirely personal in nature and therefore do not affect public peace or tranquillity and where it feels that quashing of such proceedings on account of compromise would bring about peace and would secure ends of justice, it should not hesitate to quash them.
In such cases, pursuing prosecution would be waste of time and energy.
Non-compoundable offences are basically an obstruction in entering into compromise.
In certain cases, the main offence is compoundable but the connected offences are not.

In the case of B.S. Joshi and others v. State of Haryana and another 2003 (4) SCC 675 the Honble Apex Court observed that even though the provisions of Section 320 Cr.P.C. would not apply to such offences which are not compoundable, it did not limit or affect the powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
The Honble Apex Court laid down that if for the purpose of securing the ends of justice, quashing Manish Bansal; Vijender Kumar Gupta ... vs Unknown on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187040640/
2 of FIR becomes necessary, section 320 Cr.P.C. would not be a bar to the exercise of power of quashing.

sentences.text: In the nutshell, the Honble Apex Court justified the exercise of powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the proceedings to secure the ends of justice in view of the special facts and circumstances of the case, even where the offences were non compoundable."

9. Reference is also made to WP(Crl) 1504/2020 Rahisuddin Madni V. Govt. of NCT of Delhi Through Standing Counsel Criminal delivered on 08.01.2021 in this context.
10.

sentences.text: Considering the above case law as also the settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as the legal heirs of deceased have settled all the disputes and have received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
11. Accordingly, both these petitions are allowed.

Consequently, FIR and proceedings emanating against these petitioners, pursuant to FIR No.373/2017 under Section 287/304A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Hari Nagar, Delhi are quashed.
Needless to say, the petitioners shall file the amended memo of parties thereby impleading informant - Sunil Kumar as respondent No.5 within a week from today.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.
